fatal_flaws: SCOPE WITHOUT SIZING FOR A ONE-OPERATOR TEAM: The plan enumerates roughly 60 work items across 7 milestones over an 80,420-line package (~160 modules, 1,525 test functions in 217 test files) and declares four 'parallel' streams (M1, M2, M4, M5), but the team is one operator plus AI agents, and this codebase's own doctrine makes the operator the serial bottleneck: every promotion requires HITL approval across 8 gates, so agent-parallel work still queues on human review. There are zero effort estimates, no beta window, and no stated minimum cut. Executed as written, everything is implicitly beta-critical and the beta does not ship in a reasonable window. The definition of done (governed loop on a stranger's repo, 30-min onboarding, giftable repo, credible demo) is achievable with roughly half the listed items.

B4.2'S CENTRAL DESIGN CONTRADICTION IS UNADDRESSED — BOUNDED VERIFICATION VS ARBITRARY STRANGER REPOS: /Users/kaizenpro/Projects/builder-II/builder_ii/verification_execution_runner.py:69-84 shows SUPPORTED_COMMAND_PROFILES contains exactly two profiles (platform_status, docs_audit), both hardcoded to `sys.executable -m builder_ii.verification_runner_entrypoints ...` with timeout_seconds=30 and step_id==profile enforced by _validate_fixed_profile (line 135). 'Promote bounded pytest_full profile: fixed argv, shell=False' for a stranger's repo is self-contradictory: a fixed argv cannot encode the target's interpreter/venv, the target may not use pytest at all, and a 30s timeout fails on any real suite — including builder-II's own 1,525-test suite, so the promoted profile could not even verify builder-II itself. The plan demotes 'timeout policy decision' to a sub-clause of one M3 bullet when it gates the entire goal (a). Worse, running an untrusted stranger repo's test suite is arbitrary code execution on the operator machine, and the plan — for a governance product whose promotion checklist includes 'HITL boundary' and 'failure mode' gates — never mentions sandboxing or trust boundaries for target-repo verification. Without resolving this design question first, the M1/M3 convergence stream builds toward an unshippable lane.
